title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning based Online Scheduling Policy for Deep Neural Network Multi-Tenant Multi-Accelerator Systems
problem: Online scheduling of DNNs in multi-tenant environments must optimize SLA satisfaction and hardware utilization while managing heterogeneous accelerators with different dataflows and memory bandwidth contention.
motivation: Cloud service providers require efficient scheduling policies to maximize SLA compliance and resource utilization when executing DNNs on multi-accelerator systems.
method: RELMAS applies deep reinforcement learning to make online scheduling decisions for DNN requests across heterogeneous accelerators including Simba and Eyeriss. The algorithm explicitly models dataflow heterogeneity across accelerators and memory bandwidth contention to optimize SLA satisfaction and cost-effectiveness.
key_novelty: A deep reinforcement learning framework for low-overhead online scheduling of DNNs in multi-tenant multi-accelerator systems that models heterogeneous accelerator dataflows and memory contention.
contributions: RELMAS: a DRL-based online scheduling algorithm for multi-tenant DNN systems with heterogeneous accelerators
Integration of accelerator dataflow heterogeneity and memory bandwidth contention into scheduling decisions
Demonstration of 173% improvement in SLA satisfaction rates compared to state-of-the-art techniques
Minimal energy overhead (less than 1.5%) for the scheduling algorithm
primary_theme: DRL-based online scheduling for multi-tenant DNN systems
